item.title: Tornado Watch Issued for Centre County
item.description: The National Weather Service has issued a tornado watch on Wednesday for a portion of central Pennsylvania, including Centre County. The watch is in effect until 8 p.m. Wednesday. Scattered hail up to ping-pong-ball size, wind gusts up to 70 mph and a few tornados are possible in the watch area. A tornado watch is issued when weather conditions could lead to the formation of severe storms or tornados, according to the NWS. item.title: State College Student Wins 1st Place, and a $250K Prize, in National Math and Science Competition
item.description: A State College Area School District student won first place on Tuesday night in a national math and science competition for high school seniors billed as the oldest and most prestigious of its kind. Connor Hill, a 17-year-old Delta High School senior, took the top honor and its accompanying $250,000 prize for his discrete geometry research project in the 85th Regeneron Science Talent Search produced by Society for Science. item.title: After 51 Years in Downtown State College, Art Fine Prepares to Close His Last Store
item.description: For more than half a century, Art Fine's footwear and clothing businesses have been a staple of downtown State College. Now he's getting ready to close up shop for the last time. Fine will close his last remaining store, Barefoot and Metro, on May 31. The shoe and women's clothing shop at 130 E. item.title: Penn State Men’s Hockey Dominates Minnesota in Big Ten Tournament Opener

item.title: 7 Penn State Wrestlers Earn No. 1 Seeds for NCAA Championships
item.description: Penn State wrestling will have 70% of its starting lineup seeded No. 1 at next week's NCAA Championships after brackets were revealed on Wednesday night. Seven Nittany Lions, each fresh off winning individual Big Ten championships, claimed the top seeds in their weight classes: Luke Lilledahl (125), Shayne Van Ness (149), PJ Duke (157), Mitchell Mesenbrink (165), Levi Haines (174), Rocco Welsh (184) and Josh Barr (197). item.description: Peppa Pig and her family are on their way to Penn State's Eisenhower Auditorium for a family-friendly musical theater performance at 6 p.m. on Thursday, March 26. item.description: Penn State President Neeli Bendapudi joined the leaders of Pennsylvania's three other state-related universities in Harrisburg on Wednesday for a state House Appropriations Committee budget hearing, where she faced at-times pointed questions and commentary about the decision to close seven Commonwealth Campuses. item.description: Tussey Mountain's owners are undertaking a regional review process that will allow for the expansion of the ski and recreation resort's lodge and other planned improvements. item.title: Former Penn State Safety Jaquan Brisker Signed by Pittsburgh Steelers
item.description: Former Penn State safety Jaquan Brisker is headed home. According to multiple reports, Brisker signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday afternoon, bringing him back to the Keystone State. He spent the previous four seasons with the Chicago Bears, totaling 342 tackles, seven sacks, four forced fumbles and four interceptions. item.title: Former Penn State DE Arnold Ebiketie Signs With Philadelphia Eagles
item.description: Another Nittany Lion is on the move. Former Penn State defensive end and current NFL linebacker Arnold Ebiketie has signed a one-year, $7.3 million deal with the Philadelphia Eagles, according to multiple reports Thursday night. Ebiketie spent the previous four seasons with the Atlanta Falcons, amassing 129 tackles, 16.5 sacks and four forced fumbles.
